title: per-model-kv-characteristics-and-pinned-version-publish-workflow
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: New model variants and extended-context weights have inconsistent KV cache behavior across sequence lengths. We need a reproducible per-model process that: (1) profiles KV cache hit rate, average KV memory footprint, and prefix reuse across a distribution of sequence lengths and batch sizes; (2) emits a signed performance profile artifact that can be published to the model catalog; (3) wires a model package manifest so that serving can pin to a compatible model+profile pair and fall back safely to a known-good variant.

Goals: Produce a deterministic profiling job and publishing pipeline that integrates with the model registry and release flow. Ensure profiles are expressive (heatmaps + scalar summaries), verifiable (checksums/signatures), and consumed by routing/runtime for pinning decisions and automated fallbacks. Ship instrumentation hooks in serving runtime to collect live-traffic telemetry for profile validation and regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible profiling job (kvmeter) that accepts a model artifact and a user-provided sequence distribution, runs automated warmup traces, and outputs a profile JSON + artifacts bundle
Profile artifact includes: sequence length histogram, KV hit/miss heatmap, avg KV size per layer, memory peak, suggested retention window, and recommended quantization compatibility tags
Model registry accepts a profile bundle and associates a profile_id to a model_version; profile bundle is signed and stored with checksum metadata
Serving runtime can read model manifest and apply pinning to the exact model_version or fallback to a compatible variant if mismatched; fallback behavior exercised in a canary integration test
End-to-end integration test: create model+profile, deploy to canary pool, run synthetic long-context workload, assert latency and MRR (miss rate reduction) meet thresholds
Docs: onboarding guide published to Confluence with sample command line, config options, and example profile interpretation
comments: 2026-02-11 - AK: Spike completed to determine feasible telemetry hooks. Verified LRU vs TTL retention semantics — LRU gives more stable hit-rate for variable-prefix traffic.
2026-02-13 - LO'C: Initial kvmeter prototype pushed (github.com/redwood-inference/kvmeter PR#412). It runs warmup traces and emits per-layer KV stats. Needs stubbing for synthetic user distributions.
2026-02-15 - PM review (Sofia B.): Requested that profile artifacts include explicit compatibility table for runtime kernel variants and quantization (int8/4-bit). Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-18 - Design (Marta V.): Suggested heatmap visualization layout for Console and a compact summary card for model catalog. Filed DES-221 for Console card design.

2026-02-20 - LO'C: Added profile signing support to registry client (RFC pending). Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry PR#89. Also added basic canary test harness that replays recorded customer trace bucket.

2026-02-22 - AK: Running extended CI with cross-model samples (LLaMA2-70B, Redtail-13B). Observed a 12% average KV miss reduction when applying recommended retention window for long-tail sequences. Planning follow-up OPT: tune batching thresholds per profile.
